name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-pulp-timer-zipdma-6w-loops-f1-fuzz
notes: trigger_writes and status_offsets repeat the values already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-irq-pulp-timer-profile.json; the entry re-checks them against the timer register map and interrupt declarations
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

f1_program_words 6 declares a six-word F1 program and f1_allow_loops admits the canonical bounded loop: `addi xN, x0, K` (K in 2..6), a body that never writes xN, `addi xN, xN, -1` and `bne xN, x0, head`.  The trip count is static, so the loop terminates; loop intervals must be disjoint, no transfer may enter a loop's interior, and a backward JAL/JALR or a non-canonical/nested loop is refused by name.  A loop repeats PCs, so the case's evidence is the reference retirement trace: prog_retires and prog_trace_count equal the reference count, prog_trace_hash (FNV-1a 32 over pc/insn/rd/wdata) equals the reference hash, and prog_pc_repeat equals the reference's repeated-PC count (prog_pc_order stays the honest strict-rise flag).  f1_allow_branches is required because the back edge is a B-type branch.  Evidence: runs/round1-f1-controlflow/.

fuzz_flows ["F1"] narrows the closed-loop batch to the F1 program flow, so every generated and mutated input is a program of the declared shape whose RVFI retirement trace is compared with the Python reference trace.  The same host/timer/DMA models are built; only the offered flow set changes.
